findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 21, and 3 for clearance verification exhibits. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical infrastructure layout with transformers, pull boxes, and underground lines, but no clearance verification exhibits are present. No engineered drawings demonstrating both 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius clearance envelopes from conductors are provided. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed electrical elements are shown and labeled with adequate scale (1" = 20'), but no clearance exhibits exist. Master Comment Report Section 02 identifies Austin Energy Design Requirements including UCM § 1.10.3 (Permanent Clearances from AE Overhead Lines) as applicable, confirming clearance compliance must be demonstrated.
findings.reasoning: The grouping specifies clearance exhibits must demonstrate code compliance showing both 7'-6" horizontal AND 15-foot radius clearance envelopes. The vision analysis confirmed no such exhibits are present. The requirement applies because proposed structures are located in areas potentially affecting existing utility easements and overhead electric lines. Austin Energy's Master Comment Report lists clearance standards as preliminary design requirements, making exhibits mandatory for land development review approval.
findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits not provided. Plans must include engineered and sealed exhibits demonstrating both 7'-6" minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors (measured from outer conductor, not pole centerline). Exhibits must be drawn to scale and included in permitted plan set.

findings.observation: Searched document set for building elevations, profile drawings, and cross-section exhibits showing clearances. No building elevation sheets exist in the primary site plan (39 sheets total). Sheet 9 shows building footprints and heights in tables (ranging from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1"), but no elevations depicting building elements. No cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances between proposed structures and existing electric facilities are present.
findings.reasoning: The grouping defines this item as applicable only when proposed structures are within required clearance zones. Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 vision confirmed the presence of overhead electric facilities on the site (5' Electric Easement, 15' Elec. & Tele. Easement, and OHE line on southern boundary). Building elevations or profile drawings are required to show clearances but are completely absent. Without these drawings, clearances cannot be verified as required by AEDC § 1.10.3.
findings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities. Submit building elevations and profile drawings showing dimensioned clearances measured from outer conductors for all building elements that could encroach on clearance zones.

applicableAreas: Building elevations and profile plans - all structures
findings.observation: Examined all site plan sheets for clearance dimensions and building element heights. Sheet 9 contains a Building Height Table showing overall structure heights, but no dimensions for building elements (roof overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) are provided. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed building FFE values are shown but no dimensional information about projecting elements. No building elevations exist. Clearance dimensions are completely absent from all drawings.
findings.reasoning: This deficiency applies because buildings on the site are in proximity to existing electric easements (Sheet 9 vision confirmed 5' and 15' Electric Easements). Without building elevations showing dimensions of overhangs, balconies, and canopies, and without clearance dimensions measured from outer conductor locations, compliance cannot be demonstrated. The absence of these dimensions represents a critical documentation gap.
findings.comment: Clearance dimensions and heights not specified for building elements. Provide detailed building elevations and profile plans with dimensioned clearances for all roof overhangs, balconies, awnings, and canopies, measured from outer conductor locations showing minimum distances of 7'-6" horizontal and 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution conductors.

findings.observation: Searched all sheets for clearance verification exhibits. No exhibits found showing either the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance or the 15-foot radius clearance envelopes. Sheet 9 vision confirmed overhead electric lines are shown along boundaries, and Sheet 31 vision confirmed overhead electric line shown on southern boundary. However, no clearance envelope diagrams exist on any sheet.
findings.reasoning: The presence of overhead distribution facilities confirmed by site vision analysis makes clearance verification mandatory. The grouping explicitly states Austin Energy requires BOTH clearance envelopes be satisfied simultaneously - these are separate envelopes with different geometric properties (7'-6" horizontal plane and 15-foot cylindrical radius). The complete absence of any clearance verification exhibits showing both envelopes means neither can be evaluated. This is distinct from EL-11.1 in that this specifically addresses the dual envelope requirement.
findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not show both required clearance envelopes. Provide engineered exhibits demonstrating BOTH: (1) 7'-6" minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from ground level at 7.5 feet horizontal distance from outer conductors, AND (2) 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending infinitely in all directions from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Both must be shown simultaneously.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 19, and 21 for explicit Point of Service labeling. Sheet 21 vision analysis stated: "A line labeled 'Underground Electric Line' is shown entering the site from the west from the 'Valley View Road' right-of-way... However, there is no specific label explicitly stating 'Service Connection Point' or detailing the connection to the off-site utility main." Sheet 9 shows transformers and lines but no explicit service connection label. Sheet 19 shows utility routing but does not highlight a specific service entry point. The underground electric line entering from Valley View Road is depicted but not labeled as the service point.
findings.reasoning: The presence of the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan and new underground electric routing from Valley View Road indicates new service. AEDC § 1.16.0(5) requires the point of service to be shown and labeled on all required plans. Vision analysis explicitly found NO label stating "Service Connection Point" or identifying the connection location. While the service entry is visible, it is not explicitly labeled or dimensioned as required, creating ambiguity about the approved service point.
findings.comment: Proposed point of service not shown and labeled on all required plan sheets. Clearly label and dimension the point of service on electrical plans, site plan, and utility plan with explicit call-out identifying it as the service connection location, including distance from property line and reference to the existing utility main.

applicableAreas: Service routing - from utility to buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines and transformers. Vision analysis confirmed electrical infrastructure including transformers and pull boxes connected via routing. Sheet 19 legend shows "E | Proposed Underground Electric." However, the vision analysis does not explicitly confirm whether the routing FROM the AE transformer (or connection point) TO the buildings is clearly shown. The relationship between service entry, transformer, and building connections is visually present but not explicitly documented as complete primary routing.
findings.reasoning: Sheet 21 is titled "Preliminary Electrical Design Plan" indicating new service design. AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires primary routing from AE transformer to building to be shown. While electrical infrastructure and routing are shown per vision analysis, the available documentation does not definitively confirm whether routing FROM transformer TO individual buildings is completely and clearly shown with labels. The term "primary routing" may refer specifically to utility-to-customer routing, which may differ from what is depicted.
findings.comment: Primary routing from AE transformer to building not clearly shown or labeled. Provide clear routing diagram showing the complete path from transformer through pull boxes to service entrance of each building. Label routing with conduit size, conductor gauge, and service voltage specifications.

applicableAreas: All electrical facilities shown on plans
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 explicitly stated: "The labels only identify the general facility type (e.g., transformer, pull box, meters). They do not identify size (e.g., pad dimensions, conduit diameter), voltage, capacity (e.g., kVA), ownership, or other specific technical specifications." Specific findings: (1) Transformers labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad" only - no kVA capacity, voltage, or ownership noted. (2) Pull Boxes labeled as "Electrical Pull Box" only - no conduit diameter or depth specified. (3) Meters labeled as "Electrical Meters" only - no voltage or amperage rating specified. (4) Underground Lines labeled as "Underground Electric Line" only - no conductor gauge, voltage, or ownership specified.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires electric facilities to be labeled with complete technical information. The grouping specifies required information: size, depth, voltage, and ownership. Vision analysis confirmed that NONE of this information is present on the labels used on Sheets 21 or 9. Labels identify facility type only, which is insufficient. The deficiency is not about whether facilities are labeled, but whether labels contain complete information per code requirements.
findings.comment: Electric facility labels missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information. Add complete technical specifications to all electrical facility labels including transformer kVA/voltage, pull box conduit size/burial depth, meter voltage/amperage, and underground line conductor gauge/voltage/burial depth. Labels must appear on all plan sheets where facilities are depicted.

findings.observation: Examined site plan for detailed electrical plans showing disconnects. Sheet 21 is the only electrical design sheet provided. Vision analysis confirmed it shows site plan with transformers, pull boxes, and underground lines - it is a site-level utility plan, not a building electrical plan. NO detailed electrical plans showing service panels, main disconnects, or riser diagrams are provided. No disconnects are shown anywhere in the document set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires disconnects to be shown on electrical plans. The grouping specifies this applies "All sites." The site plan contains only site-level utility routing, not building-level electrical details. If the scope includes customer electrical facilities per AEDC § 1.16.0, building-level service disconnects should be documented. Their complete absence represents a deficiency in the electrical documentation package.
findings.comment: Disconnects not shown and labeled on electrical plans. Provide electrical plans showing the location of main service disconnect(s) for each building clearly labeled with amperage rating and voltage. Show the relationship between outdoor transformers/meters and indoor disconnect locations with routing information.

findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 3 Legend found: "Existing Transformer Pad (symbol), Existing Overhead Electric Line (--- OHE ---), Proposed Transformer Pad (Square symbol with 'T')." Vision of Sheet 21 found: "There are direct text labels (callouts) pointing to specific features... 'Electrical Pull Box,' 'Electrical Transformer Pad,' 'Electrical Meters,' 'Underground Electric Line.' There is no separate, dedicated legend or symbol key box present on this sheet." Vision of Sheet 19 confirmed legend showing "[T Symbol] | Transformer Pad" and "E | Proposed Underground Electric." DISCREPANCY: Legend on Sheet 3 defines Transformer Pad as a square symbol with "T", but Sheet 21 uses TEXT CALLOUTS ("Electrical Transformer Pad") instead of the defined symbol.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires legend symbols to match actual symbols used in plans. The issue is whether text callouts are acceptable alternatives to defined symbols. Sheet 3's Legend defines specific symbols, but actual plans use TEXT CALLOUTS instead. This creates ambiguity about whether callouts are alternative identification methods or whether symbols should be used per legend. The plans do not consistently use either the symbols defined in the legend or provide alternative legend definitions for the text callouts used.
findings.comment: Legend symbols do not clearly match symbols actually used in plans. Clarify legend consistency: either standardize on use of legend symbols (e.g., 'T' symbol, '--- OHE ---' notation) on all plans, or provide alternative legend defining text callouts used (e.g., "Electrical Transformer Pad," "Electrical Pull Box"). Ensure consistent symbol and label use across all sheets.

findings.observation: Searched Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and related sheets for projected electrical load information. Sheet 21 shows utility notes mentioning water and wastewater specifications but NO electrical load information. No kW or kVA load calculations are shown. No service amperage or voltage specifications are documented. No electrical one-line diagram or load calculation documentation exists. Master Comment Report lists UCM § 1.9.3 (Installation of Metering Equipment) as a preliminary design requirement, suggesting service design details should be provided.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires projected load for electric service. The grouping specifies this applies "Only for projects with new or upgraded electric service." The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan and routing of new underground electric service indicate new service is provided. If new service is proposed, load must be documented. However, applicability is UNCLEAR because whether this qualifies as "new service" requiring load documentation in site plan versus preliminary routing subject to later building permit design is ambiguous. Master Comment Report's inclusion of metering equipment requirements suggests loads should be specified.
findings.comment: Projected load required for electrical service not clearly provided. If new service is being provided, submit load calculations and electrical demand projections in kVA or kW with service voltage, transformer size (kVA), and amperage rating specifications. Confirm with Austin Energy whether load calculations are required in site plan or deferred to building permit design.
